sanskrit: namo 'stu nīlaśikhaṇḍāya sahasrākṣāya vājine | atho ye asya satvānas tebhyo 'ham akaraṃ namaḥ ||
english: Homage be to the blue-crested one, the thousand-eyed, the swift; and likewise to his host of attendants — to them too I have rendered homage.

sanskrit: namāṃsi ta āyudhāya- -anātatāya dhṛṣṇave | ubhābhyām akaraṃ namo bāhubhyāṃ tava dhanvane ||
english: Homage to your weapon, to the bow unstrung, to the bold one; homage I have rendered to both your arms, and to your bow.

sanskrit: pra muñca dhanvanas pary ubhayor ātnyor jyām | yāś ca te hasta iṣavaḥ parā tā bhagavo vapa ||
english: Release the bowstring from both tips of the bow; and the arrows that are in your hand — scatter those away, O blessed one.

sanskrit: avatatya dhanus tvaṃ sahasrākṣa śateṣudhe | niśīrya śalyānāṃ mukhā śivo naḥ śambhur ā cara ||
english: Having unstrung the bow, O thousand-eyed, O hundred-quivered one, shattering the heads of the arrow-shafts — come to us as benign, as bringer of joy.

sanskrit: vijyaṃ dhanuḥ śikhaṇḍino viśalyo bāṇavām̐ uta | aneśann asyeṣavaḥ śivo asya niṣaṅgatiḥ ||
english: The bow of the crested one is without its string, and he is free of arrows, quiverless; his arrows are without venom, benign is his quiver.

sanskrit: pari te dhanvano hetir asmān vṛṇaktu viśvataḥ | atho ya iṣudhis tava- -āre asmin ni dhehi tam ||
english: May the missile of your bow encompass us on all sides as a protection; and your quiver — place it far off from this one.

sanskrit: yā te hetir mīḍhuṣṭama haste babhūva te dhanuḥ | tayā tvaṃ viśvato asmān ayakṣmayā pari bhuja ||
english: The bolt that was in your hand, the bow that was yours, O most bountiful — with that weapon guard us on all sides, keeping us free from disease.

sanskrit: supārśvā kāmadughā na āgañ chataudanā payasā pinvamānā | ūrjaṃ duhānā anapasphurantī yajamānasya pra tiranty āyuḥ ||
english: The well-flanked, wish-yielding hundred-cooked-rice-offering has come to us, swelling with milk; milking forth vital strength, without stumbling, it prolongs the life of the sacrificer.

sanskrit: gṛbhṇāmi medhyām uśatīṃ svastaya ūrjasvatīm anamīvāṃ svādhyām | viśvo loko mama deveṣv astu śataudanāṃ śraddadhānaḥ pacāmi ||
english: I seize her who is fit for sacrifice, who is eager, who brings well-being, who is replete with vitality, free from disease, worthy of meditation; may my whole world be among the gods — believing, I cook the hundred-rice-portion.

sanskrit: badhāna devīm abhi dhehi muñjatīṃ śataudanāṃ kāmadughā hy eṣā | maināṃ hiṃsīr aśmanā jahṛṣāṇo 'py etu devām̐ ati gacchati dviṣaḥ ||
english: Bind and apply the goddess, the muñja-grass-girt hundred-rice-offering — for she is the wish-yielding one; do not injure her with the stone in your exuberance: she passes to the gods beyond the enemy.

sanskrit: ā rabhasva brahmaṇā vaiśvadevīṃ śataudanāṃ śatapāpmāno asyāḥ | samarpayann aśmanā parvatena svargaṃ lokam adhi rohayainam ||
english: Seize with the sacred formula this all-divine hundred-rice-offering — a hundred sins are hers to absorb; pressing with the stone as with a mountain, cause him to ascend above to the heavenly world.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṇu hy enāṃ vikṛtā vikṛntann apaghnaṃś carmerayā saṃ sṛjainām | virājo duhiterayā samaktā kāmaṃ kāmaṃ yajamānāya duhām ||
english: Boldly cutting and slicing it into pieces, driving away evil, mix it with the skin-ladle; anointed by means of this daughter of Virāj, may she milk desire upon desire for the sacrificer.

sanskrit: yathāparu viśasannāti maṃsthāḥ kṛṇuṣvā me nāvadheyāni pṛthak | agan devān mānuṣī yā purābhūc chataudanā pururūpā suvarṇā ||
english: Even as you cut joint by joint, do not tarry; make the portions for me separately; she who formerly was human, the hundred-rice-offering of many forms and golden hue, has gone to the gods.

sanskrit: dvipād dvihastaḥ puruṣo mahādamo vanaspatiṃ bibharti sāyakāgram | tena parūṃṣi pravidvān aghnyāyāḥ śataudanāṃ devīṃ śatadhā vy asya ||
english: The two-footed, two-handed man, the great subduer, bears the tree-piece with its knife-tip at the front; with it, skilled, he shall carve apart the joints of the inviolable one — sunder the divine hundred-rice-offering into a hundred parts.

sanskrit: etaṃ bradhnaṃ carmaṇaḥ kṛnta sādhu tam u pramāya śatadhā vy asya | sam ut sṛjann avadhānāni sarvā rāyaspoṣaṃ yajamānāya dhehi ||
english: Cut this reddish piece from the skin well, and having measured it, divide it into a hundred parts; releasing all the portions together, bestow abundance of wealth upon the sacrificer.

sanskrit: ṛcā kumbhīm adhy agnau śrayāmi bhūmyāṃ tvā bhūmim adhi dhārayāmi | apo māṃsaṃ bibhratī mā vyathiṣṭhā mā tvā vadhiṣur menibhiḥ piśācāḥ ||
english: With the Ṛc-verse I place the pot upon the fire; I set you upon the earth, above the earth; bearing the flesh in the waters, do not tremble; may the Piśācas not slay you with their weapons.

sanskrit: ūrdhva prehi mā saṃ vikthā vy asya rajo antaram | rakṣāṃsi sarvā tīrtvā- -athā roha divaṃ tvam ||
english: Rise upward, do not collapse; spread out the inner atmosphere; having crossed beyond all the Rākṣasas — then ascend to heaven.

sanskrit: divaṃ prehi śataudane sahasrasyāyanaṃ bhava | ayutaṃ prayutaṃ bhava- -akṣitir bhavatāt tvaṃ svargaṃ lokam āruhaḥ ||
english: Go to heaven, O hundred-rice-offering; become the path for a thousand; become ten thousand, become a hundred thousand — be inexhaustible: thus you shall mount the heavenly world.

sanskrit: śataudanāṃ śatadhā bhakṣayanti śataṃ rohān rohati yo dadāti | vāmadevyaṃ naudhasam asyāḥ pakṣau tṛtīye nāke adhi viṣṭapi śritā ||
english: They partake of the hundred-rice-offering in a hundred ways; he who gives her ascends a hundred rungs; the Vāmadevya and the Naudhasa are her two wings — established on the third vault, she abides above the firmament.

sanskrit: śataudanāṃ śatadhā kalpamānā śataṃ rūpāṇi kṛṇute svaryatī | sā no devī suhavā śarma yacchatv atho mṛḍātīdṛśe ||
english: The hundred-rice-offering, arranging itself in a hundred ways, fashions a hundred forms as she goes to the sky; may that goddess, easy to invoke, grant us shelter, and likewise grant ease to those in such condition.

sanskrit: śataudanā dvādaśāhena saṃmitā śataṃ pṛṣṭhāni sasṛje svaryatī | sarvān yajñān pariyatī parastāt sā dātāraṃ rāyaspoṣe dadhātu ||
english: The hundred-rice-offering, measured out with the twelve-day rite, has created a hundred Pṛṣṭha-hymns as she traverses the sky; encompassing all sacrifices beyond, may she establish the giver in abundance of wealth.

sanskrit: abhi prehi śataudana ījānān somasatvanaḥ | yajñāṃs tvaṃ sarvān āptvā kāmaprasyāyanaṃ bhava ||
english: Go toward the soma-pressing sacrificers who have offered oblations, O hundred-rice-offering; having pervaded all sacrifices, become the pathway to the fulfillment of desire.

sanskrit: abhi prehi śataudane yajñenāyajvanas tara | ā devayūn arūruho yatrādas tridivaṃ divaḥ ||
english: Go forward, O hundred-rice-offering; with sacrifice pass beyond those who have not sacrificed; you have climbed up to the gods, to where you shine on high in the triple heaven.

sanskrit: īrāpadī prathamā śataudanā satyaṃ ha madhyam amṛtaṃ śiras tava | ubhe devī rodasī ā pṛṇāsi ||
english: The first hundred-rice-offering has the nourishment-footed one as its base; truth is indeed your middle, immortality is your crown; O goddess, you fill both the worlds.

sanskrit: ṛtaṃ ha śroṇī uta sakthau tanvā- -ojo ha bāhū uta tad balāya kam | anuṣṭhu jaṭharam ād u pārśve sarvām̐l lokāṃ chataudanā samāpa ||
english: Order indeed are the hips, and the thighs in the body; power indeed are the arms, and that serves for strength; the belly follows the due course, and further the flanks — the hundred-rice-offering has reached all the worlds.

sanskrit: cakṣuṣmatī prathamā śataudanā sūryo ha cakṣur uta candramās tava | viśvair devair ṛtubhiḥ saṃvidānā sā dātāraṃ tṛptyā tarpayāsi ||
english: The first hundred-rice-offering is endowed with sight; the sun is indeed your eye, and the moon also; in accord with all the gods and with the seasons, you, O goddess, shall satiate the giver with satisfaction.

sanskrit: śataṃ payāṃsi śatam asyā vatsāḥ śatadhā pakvāṃ vi bhajanty enām | sapta lokā divy ārpitā ye tāṃ jigetha prathamā śataudane ||
english: A hundred are her milkings, a hundred her calves; they distribute her, cooked, in a hundred shares; the seven worlds established in heaven — these you have won, O first of the hundred-rice-offerings.
